original_metadata.title: Sharp automorphism-pseudogroup bound of (n+1) squared for real bi-decomposable Monge-Ampere systems with transverse Lagrangian pairs on contact manifolds of dimension2n+1, n>=3
original_metadata.author: Goo Ishikawa; Yoshinori Machida
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof first recovers the transverse Lagrangian pair from the differential system using effective forms and the author Plucker-coordinate uniqueness argument. It then identifies the adapted contact G-structure, computes the full positive Tanaka prolongation to be zero and supplies an explicit projective transformation group attaining the bound for a constant nonzero Hessian equation.

proof_review.note: Complete Theorem5.3 and essential Theorems3.2/3.8, Proposition3.9/Lemma3.10, G-structure Proposition5.1 and prolongation Lemma5.2 read. Section8.1 gives the constant nonzero Hessian model, its contact/Monge-Ampere forms and the explicit dimension(n+1)^2 projective symmetry group preserving them, so sharpness is bundled rather than presumed. Lagrangian subbundles are transverse and nonvanishing bi-decomposition is part of the hypothesis; no integrability of the pair or flatness of the general system is added. Prior Tanaka finiteness and symplectic effective-form theorem are identified background. The decomposable-system bound, n=2 examples and homogeneous-geometry variants are not counted.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem5.3: smooth real contact manifold(M,D) of dimension2n+1 with n>=3, and a locally bi-decomposable Monge-Ampere exterior system with transverse Lagrangian pair as defined in Section2. Its local automorphism pseudogroup has dimension at most(n+1)^2; the constant nonzero Hessian model realizes equality. This is not an infinite-dimensional global diffeomorphism-group bound or an n=2 result.
original_metadata.source_boundary_note: The full original sharp symmetry Theorem 5.3 is supplied as one main problem unit with the complete new generator and Lagrangian-pair recovery, Plucker uniqueness, adapted G-structure and vanishing-prolongation proofs. The constant nonzero Hessian model, its contact and Monge-Ampere forms and explicit dimension (n+1)^2 symmetry group preserving them are bundled to prove the sharpness clause. The hypothesis is n>=3, a transverse Lagrangian pair and nonvanishing bi-decomposition; neither integrability nor flatness is imposed on the general system. Tanaka finiteness, symplectic effective-form and prior Lagrangian-contact structure results remain cited established prerequisites. Supporting results are uncounted core; the decomposable-system bound, n=2 examples and other homogeneous models are not selected.
